pr.title: Remove more `PtrToPtr` casts in GVN
pr.description:
This addresses two things I noticed in MIR:

1. `NonNull::<T>::eq` does `(a as *mut T) == (b as *mut T)`, but it could just compare the `*const T`s, so this removes `PtrToPtr` casts that are on both sides of a pointer comparison, so long as they're not fat-to-thin casts.

2. `NonNull::<T>::addr` does `transmute::<_, usize>(p as *const ())`, but so long as `T: Thin` that cast doesn't do anything, and thus we can directly transmute the `*const T` instead.

r? mir-opt
pr.author: scottmcm

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's binary simplification simplified both operands, then folded the BinOp or built `Value::BinaryOp`; it did not generally look through matching `PtrToPtr` casts on both sides of pointer comparisons. Cast simplification composed `PtrToPtr`-then-`PtrToPtr`, but had no `PtrToPtr`-then-`Transmute` composition. The old `PtrMetadata` handling compared pointee metadata/tail via `ptr_metadata_ty_or_tail`, and `UnOp::PtrMetadata` computed the metadata type locally.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical behavior was a missed optimization/no-op, not a confirmed miscompile: redundant `PtrToPtr` casts remained in pointer comparisons and before `Transmute`. The unsafe generalization to avoid is removing `PtrToPtr` from both comparison sides without requiring identical source pointer types and matching metadata, or collapsing `PtrToPtr` into `Transmute` when the cast changes metadata (fat-to-thin) and therefore pointer size/layout.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR after inlining, with pointer/reference-typed operands: pointer comparisons (`Eq`, `Ne`, `Lt`, `Le`, `Gt`, `Ge`) where both operands are GVN values of kind `Cast { kind: PtrToPtr, .. }`, and `Transmute` whose operand is a `PtrToPtr` cast. Pointees may be thin or unsized (arrays, slices), generic, or have metadata that only compares equal after normalization.
analysis.summary: GVN optimization removing redundant `PtrToPtr` casts around pointer comparisons and before `Transmute`, guarded by identical source pointer types and matching pointee metadata. Not a confirmed miscompile fix; historically these were missed optimizations. Regression tests include positive and negative controls for thin/fat and differing source types.
analysis.trigger: GVN simplifies a pointer `BinaryOp` and both operands resolve to `Value::Cast { kind: PtrToPtr, .. }` with the same source type and matching metadata; or `simplify_cast` sees `Transmute` over `PtrToPtr` with unchanged metadata; or sees nested `PtrToPtr` where the inner source type equals the outer target type.
preconditions: Both comparison operands are `PtrToPtr` casts with identical source pointer types: `lhs_from == rhs_from`.
`self.pointers_have_same_metadata(*lhs_from, lhs_ty)` succeeds, either by exact metadata type equality or successful `try_normalize_erasing_regions` normalization.
For `PtrToPtr`-then-`Transmute`, `self.pointers_have_same_metadata(inner_from, inner_to)` must hold so the cast did not change metadata or pointer size.
For nested `PtrToPtr`, only return the inner value directly when `inner_from == to`; otherwise continue with the composed cast.
Operand replacement must use `try_as_operand` and only update the MIR operand when conversion succeeds.
`PtrMetadata` uses `pointee_metadata_ty_or_projection`, which returns exact pointee metadata or a projection through `ptr::Pointee` when generic.
pitfalls: Do not remove casts merely because both sides are `PtrToPtr`; different source types such as `*mut u8` versus `*mut u32` must remain, as shown by the unoptimized `Eq([[M1]], [[M2]])` test.
Fat-to-thin casts such as `*mut [u32]` to `*const u32` change metadata and pointer layout; they must not be treated like thin pointer casts. The test keeps `Eq([[M3]], [[M4]])`.
A `PtrToPtr`-then-`Transmute` may be collapsed only when metadata is unchanged. This is why the thin case collapses to `_1 as usize (Transmute)` while the fat case retains its intermediate cast.

Generic metadata may require normalization; comparing only syntactic metadata types can miss valid cases. `pointers_have_same_metadata` first checks equality, then tries `try_normalize_erasing_regions`.
When `simplify_binary` replaces operands with cached values, keep the MIR operands and GVN value indices synchronized using `try_as_operand`.
Do not skip operand simplification side effects: the historical comment warns to only short-circuit after calling `simplify_operand` on both operands.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused `EMIT_MIR` tests under `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` with checks for both positive and negative cases: `m2 == m3` should become `Eq([[P2]], [[P3]])` after matching casts are removed; `m1 == m2` must stay `Eq([[M1]], [[M2]])` because the source types differ; `m3 == m4` must stay `Eq([[M3]], [[M4]])` because it is thin/fat. Add a transmute test: thin `thin as *const ()` followed by transmute should collapse to `_1 as usize (Transmute)`, while the fat pointer must retain its intermediate cast. Also cover generic metadata and the array-bound comparison reuse (`Lt(_1, const N)` once, `_10 = _3`) under both panic-abort and panic-unwind. The patch supplies expected MIR diffs but does not claim execution.
